lesson_title: Big Times Small, Piece by Piece
hook_text: 345 loaves a day for 28 days. Six small sums give you the answer.
clip_script: A bakery in Soweto: 345 loaves a day. How many in 28 days? Split 345 into 300, 40 and 5. Split 28 into 20 and 8. Six boxes. 300 times 20, 6 000. 40 times 20, 800. 5 times 20, 100. 300 times 8, 2 400. 40 times 8, 320. 5 times 8, 40. Add them: 9 660 loaves. In columns it is two rows. Row one: 345 times 8 is 2 760. Row two: a zero first, then 345 times 2: 6 900. Add: 9 660. Same answer. Estimate: 300 times 30 is 9 000. Close. Split, multiply every piece, add, and estimate.
visual_style: A grid of six boxes filling with products, then folding into two rows of long multiplication.
mood: Warm and steady, like bread coming out of the oven tray by tray.
pacing: Fill the six boxes quickly, fold into two rows, then the estimate as the final check.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and work out how many loaves the bakery bakes in 31 days.
